tables.title: Effect of low-power modes to I2C
tables.text_helper: Table 121, "Effect of low-power modes to I2C", in section 25.5 (I2C in low-power modes) on page 726. Columns: Mode, Description. 3 data row(s). Notes: 1. Refer to Section 25.3: I2C implementation for information about the Stop modes supported by each instance. If the wake-up from a specific stop mode is not supported, the instance must be disabled b.

rows: No effect. I2C interrupts cause the device to exit the Sleep mode.

The contents of I2C registers are kept.
– WUPEN = 1 and I2C is clocked by an internal oscillator (HSI48). The address 
recognition is functional. The I2C address match condition causes the device to exit the 
Stop mode.
– WUPEN = 0: I2C must be disabled before entering Stop mode.
The I2C peripheral is powered down. It must be reinitialized after exiting Standby mode.
notes: 1. Refer to Section 25.3: I2C implementation for information about the Stop modes supported by each instance. If the wake-up from a specific stop mode is not supported, the instance must be disabled before entering that specific Stop mode.
